newsitem.title: FRANCE: French oil pipeline halts for inspection next week.
newsitem.headline: French oil pipeline halts for inspection next week.

text.p: A French oil products pipeline linking Fos-sur-Mer near Marseille to Lyon will close next week for several days for routine inspection, an official with the pipeline operator said on Wednesday.
The pipeline is the main axis linking an area containing several refineries with France's second largest city and has average daily throughput of 28,800 cubic metres per day.
The official with operator TMR said there would be no disruption to deliveries because the inspection, of a kind required by law every 10 years, had long been anticipated.
"It will be down for maybe a week. It means a little bit of juggling but there will be no direct impact," he said.
He denied oil market rumours that the pipeline had closed and said all operations appeared to be running as normal this week.

An official at the BP refinery at Lavera, part of the area which supplies the pipeline, said some rescheduling was expected. But the company had organised alternatives and foresaw no problem in supplying its markets.
The official gave no indication whether any product would be re-exported by sea or how far trains and trucks would be used.
The BP refinery is a customer of the TMR pipeline and has processing capacity of 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude.
Other nearby refineries include Shell's 128,000 bpd Berre refinery, Esso France's 110,000 bpd Fos refinery and the 130,000 bpd Total plant at La Mede.

It was not immediately clear which of these other refineries normally depends on the TMR pipeline, which industry officials described as the main pipeline but not the only one serving the Rhone valley market.
